qualitative.gate_3m_moat_note: Proprietary file formats (.psd, .ai, .indd, PDF) and deep creative workflow lock-in support ~88% gross margins and 40%+ median ROIC; primary erosion threats stem from generative AI diffusion models and browser-native collaborative tools (Canva, Figma).
qualitative.note: Fails Gate 4 (CAP = 5, REJECT). Enterprise creative and document SaaS leader facing severe terminal disruption under Macrotrend #1 (Automation & Cognitive Tech / AI Disruption). Generative AI diffusion models (Midjourney, Flux, Stable Diffusion) and browser-native tools (Canva, Figma) commoditize routine asset creation, compress agency/enterprise seat counts, and pressure pricing power. Downstream gates halted by strict waterfall, though management would also trigger Gate 5 red flags (FTC lawsuit over deceptive dark cancellation patterns settled for $150M and $1B cash breakup fee burned on aborted $20B Figma panic bid).
qualitative.evidence: 10-year median ROIC of 40.1% (FY2025 GAAP ROIC of 61.7%) and pristine ~88% gross margins reflect historic creative workflow dominance. FY2025 revenue reached $23.77B with $8.71B EBIT and $10.03B OCF ($7.91B Owner FCF, 111.7% conversion). However, the core seat-based model faces severe structural headwinds: (1) Generative AI models automate routine digital asset generation, threatening seat expansion at enterprise customers; (2) Browser-native design leader Figma out-innovated Adobe XD in UI/UX, leading to an aborted $20B acquisition that cost $1B in cash breakup fees; (3) The FTC/DOJ sued Adobe for deceptive dark patterns and hidden early termination fees on subscriptions, settled in March 2026 for $150M ($75M penalty + $75M relief), violating customer value-for-money; (4) Balance sheet remains sound ($5.4B cash vs $6.2B long-term debt), but terminal advantage period is compressed to 5 years (CAP < 15 threshold), triggering immediate rejection at Gate 4.
